external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Each user belongs to one company and is either an admin or a viewer. Users authenticate with an email address, password, and session cookie; there is no second factor.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The person who receives an invoice email and views the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
external_entities.notes: The payment page asks the payer to sign in to nothing.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A support employee who uses the admin console from the support office network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Each agent signs in to the admin console with their own account and a one-time code.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users, which manages invoices, customer information, payout bank details, PDF jobs, and payment pages.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app
processes.notes: The app adds the company filter to each query itself. It loads invoices by invoice number, saves every field received from the invoice edit form, and uses one database account and one bucket service credential for all companies.

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A worker that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes rendered PDFs to the PDF bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
processes.notes: It trusts the company ID carried by the job.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: The console used by support agents to open sessions in the billing app as customer users.
processes.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
processes.notes: The admin console is reachable only from the support office network.

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The database has no row-level security, and the app connects with one database account for all companies. The source does not state how the database is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue carrying PDF render jobs with a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state how the queue is reached or protected at rest.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared cloud bucket holding rendered invoice PDFs under company IDs and invoice numbers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_stores.notes: The billing app fetches PDFs with one service credential for all companies. The source does not state how the bucket is protected at rest.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: A customer user uses the billing app to access and modify invoicing data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.notes: Users authenticate with an email address and a password and get a session cookie. There is no second factor, for admins or viewers.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie; second factor: none
data_flows.data_description: invoices, customer information, and payout bank details

data_flows.name: view payment page
data_flows.description: A payer follows an invoice link and views the invoice payment page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details
data_flows.notes: The payment page asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.data_description: invoice, company name, and bank details

data_flows.name: send invoice link
data_flows.description: The billing app sends an invoice email containing a link ending in the invoice number to the payer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: invoice link ending in the invoice number

data_flows.name: manage invoice data
data_flows.description: The billing app reads and writes invoices, customers, and payout bank details in the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database
data_flows.notes: The app applies the company filter itself and uses one database account for all companies.
data_flows.data_description: invoices, customer information, and payout bank details

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a PDF render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue
data_flows.notes: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: consume render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
data_flows.data_description: company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads an invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID carried by the job.
data_flows.data_description: invoice identified by company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes the rendered PDF to the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_flows.data_description: rendered invoice PDF

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.notes: Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.
data_flows.authentication: one service credential for all companies
data_flows.data_description: rendered invoice PDF

data_flows.name: sign in to console
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code
data_flows.data_description: support agent account credentials and one-time code

data_flows.name: open customer session
data_flows.description: The admin console opens a billing-app session as any customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: Actions are recorded in the tenant database against the customer user rather than the support agent.
data_flows.data_description: customer-user session

data_flows.name: record customer actions
data_flows.description: The billing app records actions performed through an agent-opened customer session in the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Everything the agent then does is recorded in the tenant database against that customer user
data_flows.notes: The records are not attributed to the support agent.
data_flows.data_description: records of actions attributed to the customer user
